data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The binary 'idempotent vs. safe' framing is insufficient. What an append-only event log actually requires is a third property: replay-determinism, where the operation's effect on the log is determined solely by its logical content, not by its invocation count or timing. This is stronger than safety (which permits benign duplicates) and more specific than general idempotency (which concerns arbitrary state, not log content specifically).","counterconditions":[{"case":"If replay-determinism is shown to be equivalent to idempotency restricted to log-content as the relevant state, this collapses into Candidate 1.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the log's replay layer normalizes entries (e.g., strips timestamps), then replay-determinism may be achieved by safe operations.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If 'published definitions' do not recognize replay-determinism as a distinct concept, this candidate lacks definitional grounding.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"An operation can be idempotent in state terms while still producing non-deterministic log entries: e.g., appending a wall-clock timestamp that differs on retry changes the log content but may not change the system's logical state. An operation can be safe while producing duplicate entries. Replay-determinism requires that the same logical operation always produces the same log entry, which neither safety nor idempotency alone guarantees without additional constraints on what the operation embeds.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
